road.name: Chiwawa River Road (FSR 6200) to Phelps Creek Road (FSR 6211)/Phelps Creek Trailhead, or FSR 6200 to Trinity Trailhead; alternatively no road needed via the Lake Chelan ferry + Holden Village approach
road.status: CLOSED as of 2026: FSR 6200 is closed from the Atkinson Flat Campground junction north to Trinity per USFS order, cutting off both Phelps Creek and Trinity trailheads from this side
road.driveNote: When open: from Leavenworth, US-2 W 15 mi to Coles Corner, WA-207 N 4.4 mi, Chiwawa Loop Rd, then FSR 6200 ~22 mi (gravel after mile 11) to Phelps Creek Rd/FSR 6211, then 2.3 mi to Phelps Creek Trailhead (3,500 ft). Rough, rutted road, not recommended for low-clearance vehicles even when fully open.

road.name: Chiwawa River Road (Forest Road 6200) to Trinity Trailhead
road.status: Closed beyond MP 18.2 (2026 season) — not a normal seasonal closure
road.driveNote: From Coles Corner (US-2) take SR-207 toward Lake Wenatchee ~4.2 mi, bear right onto Chiwawa Loop Road, then left onto Chiwawa River Road (FR 6200); pavement ends near mile 10.8, and the final stretch is rough gravel/dirt not suited to low-clearance vehicles. As of 2026 the road is closed to vehicles at MP 18.2 beyond Atkinson Flat Campground — plan for extra road-walking miles to reach Trinity Trailhead.
road.seasonalGate: Normally opens as snow clears in late May/June and stays open into fall; currently closed beyond Atkinson Flat under USFS closure order #06-17-07-2026-11 (effective May 20, 2026 through December 31, 2027 unless rescinded sooner) after December 2025 storm damage, rather than a routine seasonal gate.

road.name: Chiwawa River Road / Forest Road 6200
road.status: paved for roughly the first 8-11 miles from Chiwawa Loop Road, then rough gravel/dirt for the final ~10-12 miles to Trinity Trailhead
road.driveNote: From Coles Corner on US-2, take WA-207 north 4.4 miles, then Chiwawa Loop Road and FR 6200 about 23 miles total to Trinity Trailhead (2,800'); the final stretch is not recommended for low-clearance vehicles.
road.seasonalGate: Usually not fully accessible until the road melts out/is cleared, often mid-to-late June. As of mid-2026 the road is additionally under an active USFS closure order (effective May 20, 2026 through Dec 31, 2027) from Atkinson Flats Campground north to Trinity, due to December 2025 storm damage — Trinity Trailhead is currently NOT reachable by vehicle. Check Wenatchee River Ranger District alerts before driving.

access.fees: $5 per vehicle per day, or $30 for an annual pass, at Trinity Trailhead.
access.rules: Glacier Peak Wilderness rule: no wood campfires above 3,500 ft elevation — this covers essentially the entire route and approach, so stoves only. Camping is also restricted within 200 ft of Lyman Lake/Holden Lake shorelines and 1/4 mile of Image Lake if approaching via those basins. Free self-issue wilderness permit required at the trailhead.
access.permit: Free self-issue Glacier Peak Wilderness permit at the trailhead; no quota or reservation system for this area.
access.closures: As of mid-2026, Forest Road 6200 is closed under an active USFS order from the Atkinson Flats Campground junction north to Trinity — Trinity Trailhead is NOT currently accessible by vehicle. The closure took effect May 20, 2026 (damage from a December 2025 storm/rain event: washouts, slides, plugged culverts) and runs through December 31, 2027 unless rescinded sooner, with no reopening estimate given. Check current Wenatchee River Ranger District alerts before planning a trip.
access.landManager: Wenatchee River Ranger District, Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest (Glacier Peak Wilderness); (509) 548-2550
access.land_manager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest (Wenatchee River Ranger District) — Glacier Peak Wilderness
access.parking_pass: Northwest Forest Pass required at some trailheads (fee day-use sites) — $5/day or $30/year.
access.passRequired: Northwest Forest Pass, Digital Day Pass, or Interagency Recreation Pass accepted at Trinity Trailhead

overnight_permit.what: Free self-issue Glacier Peak Wilderness permit
overnight_permit.where: Fill one out at the trailhead kiosk (Phelps Creek, Trinity, Entiat River, or the Holden trailheads). Holden Village and its access road are closed to hikers through at least summer 2026.

access.rules: Leave No Trace; standard Glacier Peak Wilderness regulations apply (group size limits, no stock in the last half-mile to Phelps Basin).
access.permit: No fee and no wilderness permit purchase required; self-issue wilderness registration may be requested at the trailhead kiosk once inside Glacier Peak Wilderness (entered at 2.6 miles on the Phelps Creek Trail).
access.closures: As of mid-2026, Chiwawa River Road (FR 6200) is CLOSED under an active USFS order (effective May 20, 2026 through Dec 31, 2027, no reopening estimate given) starting at the Atkinson Flat Campground junction and continuing north -- well before reaching Phelps Creek Road/FR 6211. The Wenatchee River Ranger District's current-conditions page lists Phelps Creek Trailhead among the affected sites and states the road is unlikely to reopen for summer 2026. This closes the standard vehicle approach to Dumbell Mountain entirely for the foreseeable future; confirm current status with the Ranger District (509-548-2550) before planning this route. The final 2.3 miles on Phelps Creek Road/FR 6211 are rough and not recommended for low-clearance vehicles even when the road is open.
access.landManager: Wenatchee River Ranger District, Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest (Glacier Peak Wilderness) — (509) 548-2550, closed Wednesdays.
access.passRequired: None required at Phelps Creek Trailhead — it is not a fee site, so no Northwest Forest Pass or Interagency Pass is needed for parking.

overnight_permit.what: Free self-issue Glacier Peak Wilderness permit
overnight_permit.where: Fill one out at the trailhead kiosk (Phelps Creek, Trinity, Entiat River, or the Holden trailheads). Holden Village and its access road are closed to hikers through at least summer 2026.

access.fees: None — Phelps Creek Trailhead is a no-fee USFS site.
access.rules: Wilderness group-size limit of 12 people/stock combined applies (forest-wide rule for Okanogan-Wenatchee wildernesses other than Lake Chelan-Sawtooth and Pasayten).
access.permit: Free self-issue wilderness permit required at the Glacier Peak Wilderness boundary (~2.6 mi up Phelps Creek Trail). No Northwest Forest Pass or trailhead fee is required at Phelps Creek Trailhead.
access.closures: IMPORTANT (current as of mid-2026): Chiwawa River Road (FR 6200) is closed to vehicles beyond Atkinson Flat Campground, north to Trinity, due to a December 2025 storm/debris-flow that damaged the roadbed. The USFS closure order runs May 20, 2026 through Dec 31, 2027 with no reopening estimate, and it currently blocks normal vehicle access to the Phelps Creek and Trinity trailheads. Check current Okanogan-Wenatchee NF alerts before driving.
access.landManager: Glacier Peak Wilderness, Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest — administered by the Wenatchee River Ranger District (not the Chelan Ranger District, which covers the Stehekin/Lake Chelan side of the wilderness).

overnight_permit.what: Free self-issue Glacier Peak Wilderness permit
overnight_permit.where: Fill one out at the North Fork Entiat, Entiat River or Phelps Creek trailhead kiosk.

road.name: Chiwawa River Road (FR 6200) to Phelps Creek Road (FR 6211)
road.status: Roughly 22 miles on FR 6200 (paved near the valley, gravel/rough further in) then about 2.3-2.5 miles on FR 6211 to road's end at the Phelps Creek Trailhead (3,500 ft); rough native-surface sections are not recommended for low-clearance vehicles. CONFIRMED CURRENT as of mid-2026: FR 6200 is closed to vehicles at milepost 18.2 (just past Atkinson Flat Campground) due to storm/debris-flow damage near the Dry Creek Bridge, effective May 20, 2026 through at least December 31, 2027 with no reopening estimate — this closure blocks the standard drive-to-trailhead approach and adds significant road-walking distance. Verify current status with the Ranger District before driving.
road.driveNote: From Leavenworth: US-2 west ~15 mi to Coles Corner, right on WA-207 north ~4.4 mi, right on Chiwawa Loop Rd (stay right at the intersection), then left onto Chiwawa River Rd/FR 6200 for ~22 mi, then right onto Phelps Creek Rd/FR 6211 for ~2.3-2.5 mi to the trailhead.
road.seasonalGate: Typically opens late spring once snow and washouts are cleared; closes with the first significant fall/winter snow

access.fees: None currently listed for the Phelps Creek Trailhead specifically
access.rules: Standard Glacier Peak Wilderness regulations apply (Leave No Trace, camp on durable surfaces, pack out waste); no red-tape beyond the self-issue permit
access.permit: Free self-issue wilderness permit at the Phelps Creek trailhead kiosk, required once you enter Glacier Peak Wilderness at 2.6 mi in; no quota or reservation
access.closures: CONFIRMED CURRENT (as of mid-2026): Chiwawa River Road (FR 6200) is closed to vehicles at milepost 18.2, just past Atkinson Flat Campground, due to a rock/debris flow that damaged the roadbed and drainage near the Dry Creek Bridge. The closure order took effect May 20, 2026 and runs through at least December 31, 2027 with no reopening estimate, per the Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest. This blocks the standard drive-in approach to the Phelps Creek Trailhead and would add roughly 6 miles of road-walking each way (about 12 miles round trip) from the closure point. Verify current status with the Wenatchee River Ranger District before driving out.
access.landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest, Wenatchee River Ranger District (509-548-2550); the route lies within Glacier Peak Wilderness
access.passRequired: Bring a Northwest Forest Pass / America the Beautiful pass for trailhead parking — the official Forest Service listing currently shows no fee at the Phelps Creek Trailhead itself, but pass requirements at Forest Service trailheads change, so carry one regardless

overnight_permit.what: Free self-issue Glacier Peak Wilderness permit
overnight_permit.where: Fill one out at the trailhead kiosk (Phelps Creek, Trinity, Entiat River, or the Holden trailheads). Holden Village and its access road are closed to hikers through at least summer 2026.

road.name: Chiwawa River Road (FR 6200) to Phelps Creek Road (FR 6211)
road.status: CLOSED as of May 20, 2026 (USFS Forest Order #06-17-07-2026-11): FR 6200 is closed to vehicles at milepost 18.2, just past Atkinson Flat Campground, after a debris flow deposited roughly 150 cubic yards of material and cut ruts near the Dry Creek Bridge. No reopening estimate has been given; the order runs effective May 20, 2026 through December 31, 2027 unless rescinded sooner. Check the Okanogan-Wenatchee NF alerts page before driving — the Phelps Creek Trailhead is currently unreachable by vehicle beyond this closure.
road.driveNote: From Coles Corner on US-2 (about 15 miles west of Leavenworth), take WA-207 north ~4.4 miles, bear right onto Chiwawa Loop Road for 0.4 mile, then right onto County Hwy 22/Chiwawa River Road for 0.8 mile to Forest Road 6200. Continue north on FR 6200 about 22 miles (paved for roughly the first half, then rough gravel) to FR 6211, then turn right and drive the rough, potholed Phelps Creek Road 2.3 miles to the trailhead (3,500 ft). Low-clearance vehicles should go slowly on the upper roads.
road.seasonalGate: Not gated, but the upper road and trailhead are typically snow-covered and impractical until roughly June; check current USFS road/trail conditions.

access.fees: $5/vehicle/day or $30 annual day-use fee at White River Trailhead; Northwest Forest Pass, Interagency Pass, or Recreation.gov Digital Day Pass accepted
access.permit: Free self-issuing wilderness permit, available at the White River Trailhead — no quota or reservation required
access.closures: CLOSED RIGHT NOW: Okanogan-Wenatchee closure order 06-17-07-2026-40 (Little Giant Fire), effective 3 September 2026 through 31 October 2026 unless rescinded sooner, closes FSR 6400 to the end of the road and lists the White River Trailhead, which is this route's access. As of mid-2026, White River Road (FR 6400) itself was not on the Wenatchee River Ranger District's storm-damage closure list, but numerous other district roads remain closed through Dec 31, 2027 following the December 2025 storm event, and Stage 1 fire restrictions are common in late summer — check current Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest alerts before driving
access.landManager: Glacier Peak Wilderness, Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest (Wenatchee River Ranger District, Leavenworth)

overnight_permit.what: Free self-issue Glacier Peak Wilderness permit
overnight_permit.where: Fill one out at the trailhead kiosk and carry it with you.

access.fees: $5/vehicle/day or $30/annual 'Digital Day Pass' at the North Fork Entiat Trailhead (payable via the Recreation.gov app or on-site), or a Northwest Forest Pass / America the Beautiful interagency pass.
access.rules: Standard National Forest rules apply (Leave No Trace). The North Fork Entiat Trailhead lot itself is day-use/no-camping, though parking there overnight while backpacking is fine.
access.permit: No wilderness permit is required. Cardinal Peak and the North Fork Entiat approach lie in general National Forest land outside designated wilderness — north of the Lake Chelan-Sawtooth Wilderness boundary (which runs close by, near Emerald/Saska Peaks) and well south of the Glacier Peak Wilderness, which is across the Entiat/White River divide.
access.closures: CLOSED RIGHT NOW: the Little Giant Fire closure, in effect through 31 October 2026 unless lifted sooner, closes the Entiat River Road (FR 5100), FR 5606, the North Fork Entiat River Trail #1437 and the Pyramid Mountain Trail #1433, which is this route's entire access. Separately, the Entiat River Road corridor (FR-51) sustained damage in the December 2025 storm event; as of spring 2026 a landslide near the upper end of the road (beyond the FR-5606 junction, near Cottonwood Campground/Entiat River Trailhead) required a high-clearance-only temporary bypass with trailers prohibited. That damage is past the FR-5606 turnoff used for Cardinal Peak, but check current Okanogan-Wenatchee NF alerts/current-conditions pages before driving.
access.landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest, Entiat Ranger District
access.passRequired: Northwest Forest Pass, Interagency (America the Beautiful) Pass, or the trailhead's $5/day Digital Day Pass — required specifically at the North Fork Entiat Trailhead

overnight_permit.what: Free self-issue Glacier Peak Wilderness permit
overnight_permit.where: Fill one out at the North Fork Entiat, Entiat River or Phelps Creek trailhead kiosk.

access.fees: Standard Okanogan-Wenatchee NF trailhead/parking fee policies apply in addition to the wilderness permit.
access.notes: Northwest Forest Pass required ($5/day or $30/annual). Free wilderness permit available (self-issue at trailhead). Day use accessible May 15 - October 31 (peak season July-September). Currently restricted due to Three Queens Fire (as of July 2026). Contact Snoqualmie Ranger District: (425) 888-1421 for current conditions.
access.permit: Self-issue, free wilderness permit at the trailhead.
access.landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest, Cle Elum Ranger District (Alpine Lakes Wilderness)
access.passRequired: Northwest Forest Pass or America the Beautiful pass typically required for trailhead parking.

access.fees: Standard Okanogan-Wenatchee NF trailhead/parking fee policies apply in addition to the wilderness permit.
access.notes: Alpine Lakes Wilderness permit required (May 15-Oct 31; self-issue at trailhead, no fee). Northwest Forest Pass or America the Beautiful Pass required. CURRENTLY CLOSED July 24-October 31, 2026 due to Three Queens Fire (Closure Order 06-17-03-2026-25). Cle Elum Ranger District: (509) 852-1100. No campfires above 5,000 ft elevation.
